title: The Inconsistent Witness
description: Three statements were given about the evening the clock stopped. Only one statement contains a detail that is physically impossible given the known layout of the Chronology Wing.
question: Which witness made a claim that cannot be true?

options.text: Witness A — claimed to hear a chime
Witness B — claimed the clock was already stopped and noted a metallic smell
Witness C — claimed the calendar date had changed

hint: The maintenance log states the chime mechanism was permanently disabled in 1987.
explanation: Witness A is the inconsistent one. The clock had no functioning chime, so no one could have heard it. The other details are possible.

title: Decode the Sequence
description: The underlined words from the first three letters, when read in order, form a short phrase. Using the simple substitution key found on the cipher card (A=N, B=O, C=P ... classic ROT13), decode the final coordinate string.
question: What is the decoded coordinate string? (Enter the letters only, no spaces)
hint: Apply ROT13 to the underlined sequence: 'A 47 R 12' becomes something useful for a map.
explanation: ROT13 of the key sequence yields N47E12 — a grid reference that matches an unlogged visitor entry.

title: Count the Figures
description: Compare the public photograph description with the negative description and the minutes.
question: How many people appear in the original glass-plate negative?
hint: The negative is the original exposure. The public print was later altered.
explanation: The original negative shows six figures. The seventh was added to the public photograph.

title: Pattern Recognition
description: The static bursts on the tape form groups that can be read as Morse code. A short segment translates to a three-letter code used by the observatory.
question: What three-letter code is encoded in the first complete group of bursts? (Uppercase)
hint: Short-long-short patterns often map to common observatory abbreviations for 'signal'.
explanation: The pattern decodes to SIG — the internal code used to mark anomalous signal events without formal logging.

title: The Missing Number
description: The catalogue jumps from 4471 to 4473. A sealed box exists with the inventory mark 4472. The 1991 audit called it a clerical error.
question: What is the most reasonable conclusion about entry 4472?

options.text: It was never assigned and the box is a later forgery
It was deliberately removed from official records while the physical material was preserved
The audit correctly identified a simple numbering mistake
The box belongs to a different institution and was misfiled

hint: The physical existence of the box and the contents describing an unlisted annex strongly suggest intentional omission rather than error.
explanation: The gap was deliberate. The documents were removed from the official catalogue but preserved in a sealed, unlisted location as a quiet failsafe.
